why: The one question, asked of every expression/predicate evaluator in the platform: what does it do with input it cannot handle? The one rule: an input the evaluator cannot handle is an error -- never a default answer. Silently returning everything, nothing, false, or null is the defect. Every instance here is individually small and individually defensible -- 'fail open so nothing disappears', 'an absent query means no filter', 'a missing path is just null'. Together they are a platform in which a declaration that does nothing looks exactly like a declaration that works. That matters more than usual here: the platform's whole direction is an AI author writing this JSON. An author who can see the wrong answer will debug it. An author who is told nothing will ship it. check-x0-evaluator-coverage.py enforces two things against this registry: a FIXED/CLEAN entry's proof test still exists and still asserts the specific behavior, and no evaluator-shaped class (evaluatorShapedGlobs) ships without a registry entry answering this question for it.
origin: Wave 0.2 of MASTER_AI_PLATFORM_PROGRAMME_v2.md Sec 2.1, opened 2026-07-31. The audit found five instances against two confirmed plus one predicted at open, and two of the five (X0-6, X0-7) were found by using the feature rather than reading it.
supersedes: docs/X0_SILENT_EXPRESSION_REGISTER.md, deleted by md-zero-2026-08-11 PLAN.md Phase 1 (the pilot for that plan): the doc was a markdown table hand-kept in parity with this JSON by a checker that read both. The JSON is the only copy now; its narrative fields below carry what the doc's prose said.

entries.note: LC-P0 (2026-07-31): applyWhere compiles the predicate and an uncompilable where throws UnsupportedPredicateException instead of passing every row. Known residual, asserted by unknownFieldStillSilentlyMatchesNothing in the same test: a typo'd but compilable field name matches nothing at this layer; ConceptValidation rejects an unknown where field at model validation, so it is caught before runtime. Registry corrected 2026-10-23: the entry still said OPEN long after the fix landed. Original finding: declared queries[].where outside one field==literal passes every row through unfiltered; tracked by LC-P0/Wave 0.3, not required to pass a must-error test yet.

entries.testExemptReason: REG-95's fix (tokenize instead of split) was verified live by an ad hoc node probe, not a committed automated test -- there is no checked-in regression test for evaluateDerived/derivedSegments, the mustache-embedded JS function itself. Recorded here explicitly (not silently passed) as a residual: this class has no regression protection against the exact bug it once shipped (filter(...), its own documented syntax, returned 0). Left open by Move 13 P6 rather than force-built -- a real fix needs a JS test harness for mustache-template-embedded code, which does not exist yet and is a bigger task than this gate.

entries.note: REG-96: ProcedureConditionEvaluator supports <ref> (== | != | > | >= | < | <=) <literal|ref>, and an unparseable condition throws UnsupportedConditionException instead of taking the else-path. An absent operand compares as null (absentOperandIsFalseNotAnError) by design. Registry corrected 2026-10-23: the entry still said OPEN long after the fix landed. Original finding: truthiness-only; '== X' is inexpressible. Tracked by REG-96, not required to pass a must-error test yet.
band transaction.visibleWhen: the only spelling the validator accepted had its predicate silently dropped before the evaluator ever saw it.

RolePermissions.toRole(): an app-defined role name that toRole() didn't recognize returned null, and the caller's loop just continue'd past it -- the role silently granted nothing, with no error anywhere. Wave 3, RC-B1.

REG-100: value refs that are about to be WRITTEN (patchConcept.set, mapList.select, mapValue, return values, computeValue operands) go through resolveStrict, which fails REF_UNRESOLVABLE for an unbound key and still accepts an explicit null already in state. Registry corrected 2026-10-23: the entry still said OPEN long after the fix landed. Original finding: resolve() returns null for an unresolvable $ref path instead of throwing (resolveSetValue's consumers: patchConcept.set/mapList.select/mapValue). Filed in the register itself, no REG id yet.
entries.detail: DefaultProcedureExecutor.resolve(state, ref) walks a dotted path and returns null the moment a segment is missing. It is the resolver behind resolveSetValue, which is what patchConcept.set, mapList.select and mapValue use -- so { "type": "patchConcept", "concept": "Lote", "id": "$loteId", "set": { "quantidade": "$item.quantidad" } } (note the typo: quantidad, not quantidade) writes quantidade: null, with no error anywhere. What makes this a finding rather than a design choice is that the same class already disagrees with itself: requireString and requireMap -- used for idRef and for map-shaped inputs -- call the same resolve and then throw IllegalArgumentException when it comes back null/blank. Id refs are loud; value refs are silent. One of the two is wrong, and nothing records which. Interaction with REG-89's history: patchConcept + createIfMissing builds a brand-new record out of set alone, so a typo'd $ref there creates a record with a null field rather than failing, and a governed gateway then rejects it for a required-field violation naming a field the author never mentioned -- the error surfaces one layer away from its cause. Same fix as X0-7: a filter/ref that cannot be resolved must be an error, never an empty/null one; both should land with LC-P0 in Wave 0.3, not separately.

entries.note: REG-100: a runQuery step that NAMES a query absent from queriesByName fails QUERY_NOT_FOUND instead of returning every row; a step that names no query is still a plain list. Registry corrected 2026-10-23: the entry still said OPEN long after the fix landed. Original finding: runQuery with a query name absent from queriesByName returns an unfiltered list. Filed in the register itself, no REG id yet. Same class as X0-6 (DefaultProcedureExecutor) -- listed separately because the register documented them as two distinct methods/findings.
entries.detail: DefaultProcedureExecutor.runQuery says so in its own comment: the query name is threaded through the (legacy-named) 'operation' slot, and when it's absent from queriesByName the result is unfiltered, same as before that fix landed. This is X0-1's exact shape one layer up: X0-1 is about a declared where that does not filter; this is about a declared query that does not filter, because the name did not resolve. It is already acknowledged in a comment, which is the most dangerous state for this class: known, written down, and not surfaced to the author. PackValidation does check that a runQuery step's query names a declared query, so the model-level door is shut -- but the runtime lookup is keyed by a normalized name and falls back to unfiltered rather than failing, so any drift between the two (pack-provided queries, a rename, a case/normalization mismatch) reopens it silently.

entries.note: evaluateVisibleWhen fails OPEN (surface stays visible) deliberately -- reasoned and accepted, not a defect: a hidden surface whose rows are still committed is worse than a visible one, so worst case something stays visible, it never disappears incorrectly and silently drops data from view. That reasoning holds. One accepted gap inside it: $root.<field> predicates aren't validated against the root concept's declared fields the way $ui.<name> now is (Move 11 W6) -- a typo validates clean and silently shows everything, forever. Bounded follow-up (validate $root.<field> predicates the same way), not required by this gate: it converts the accepted fail-open from a hazard into a genuinely safe default.
enabledWhen (business-ui evaluateWhen), same grammar/family/rationale as X0-8, including its accepted $root.<field> validation gap.

computeValue refuses an unknown operator at MODEL level (PackValidation), by name, with the legal set, at authoring time -- no runtime default, no silent answer. This is the shape every other row above should converge on.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23) of the runtime-support expression engine; this entry used to claim the whole runtime-support directory with verdict NOT_AUDITED, which also satisfied the glob check for every file in it. Syntax side fails closed and is not the defect: an expression neither ComputedExpression nor the legacy matcher understands is a violation ('unsupported expression format'), never a pass; an unknown invariant ref is INVARIANT_UNKNOWN_REF. The defect is the lookup side: NO_UNIQUE_CHECKER / NO_COMPOUND_UNIQUE_CHECKER / NO_CONFLICT_CHECKER / NO_SCOPE_CHECKER all return false, so an engine built without a lookup answers 'no duplicate' / 'no conflict' / 'not found' instead of saying it cannot check -- live in the flow engine's invariantEngine bean (no lookups) and for compound unique in CRUD (the RuntimeHost factory drops the lookup). Also evaluate(entityName, payload) returns no violations for an unknown entity. See REG-283.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23): builds its delegate with CelInvariantEngine.fromCompiledModel(model) -- no unique, conflict or scope lookup -- and is the invariantEngine bean KernelRunner/InvariantCheckStep use, so flow checkInvariants get X0-11's default answers. See REG-283.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23): evaluateSchemaExpression returns null for anything it cannot evaluate, by design ('a malformed expression still yields null at record-save time instead of throwing'); for a derivedExpression the caller then removes the field. Model validation accepts any call syntax, so a typo'd function in a derivedExpression validates clean and erases the field on every save. See REG-284.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23): the non-strict evaluate(expression, data) -- the defaultExpression path of the governed semantic policy -- evaluates with an EMPTY function registry and returns the expression's own TEXT on ExpressionException. Reproduced: evaluate("concat(first, ' ', last)", ...) returns "concat(first, ' ', last)". The $user overload and evaluateStrict are not affected (the first registers ValueExpressionFunctions.base() and rethrows for a real actor; the second throws). See REG-284.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23): access.read/access.write and $user lifecycle guards. A MALFORMED rule fails closed (false = deny), correctly. But an unbound $user.<name> resolves to null and validation lets any $-name through, so the rule answers against null: evaluate("ownerId == $user.idd", {ownerId:null}, anonymous) is true -- a typo can grant. See REG-285.

REG-282 audit (2026-10-23): toRuntimeOrchestration returns null -- and registerOrchestrationSubscribers skips the rule with no log -- when any one action cannot be built (unknown type/concept, missing entityManager/dataSource/dispatcher, blank fields), discarding the rule's buildable actions too. evaluateOrchestrationCondition falls back to a legacy ==/!= substring matcher on a condition that does not parse. See REG-286.

having (LC-B1), proposed. Must be born loud -- when it is authored, it needs a registry entry with verdict FIXED/CLEAN and a real must-error test in the SAME commit, not added here in advance of the code existing. Rule for anything added later, not just this one: a new evaluator, subset, or predicate dialect must answer this register's one question before it ships.
